questions.q: Which crate pair exists so extension authors can compile goose contracts without pulling the engine?
explanation: goose-cli/goose-mcp sit at the top of the dependency stack, not the bottom.

cargo warns and picks one direction automatically
Only the two cyclic crates fail, others build

It validates the role against a whitelist
explanation: Serde doesn't compress; the custom function migrates shapes.

questions.q: Config layering in goose works because:
options: Config holds an ordered config_paths list — later files override earlier ones, writes go to the last
Config polls the filesystem on every read
There is only ever one config file

questions.q: `Config::global()` returns &'static Config, meaning:
options: One OnceCell-initialized process-wide singleton with a stable reference
A fresh instance for each caller
explanation: It memoizes, so repeat calls share the instance.

Nothing is fetched over the network.

questions.q: Which crate owns StateMachine, Step, Operation in v1.49.0?
options: goose-agent, re-exported through goose's state_machine module
explanation: agent.rs builds the step list but doesn't define the executor types.
goose-mcp is MCP servers only.
rmcp is the protocol implementation.

questions.q: A parity gap means:

API version drift between UI and core

UI/core drift is a different concern.
Lockfiles don't create behavior gaps between loops.

questions.q: In the Provider trait, `complete()` is:

questions.q: `estimate_model_cost` computes cost from:

questions.q: Streaming most commonly breaks when:

questions.q: Which stone splits an inspector's findings into verdict buckets?

questions.q: An extension's disallowed env keys exist because:

As soon as its manifest exists on disk
Only after a session is archived

questions.q: `get_prefixed_tools` solves:

Search ranking is chat_history_search's concern.

questions.q: Why does goose wrap rmcp's client in its own McpClient?
options: To add capabilities tracking, structured errors, cancellation, and tool-call enrichment behind McpClientTrait
explanation: rmcp ships a client; goose intercepts via ClientHandler.
stdio/sse transports are used deliberately.

questions.q: A dangling $ref in a tool schema is handled by:
options: inline_refs, which inlines definitions for providers that can't resolve refs
explanation: The network never repairs schema text.
Ignoring schemas would break tool calling.
Session naming doesn't touch schemas.

questions.q: What does `collapse_const_unions` normalize?

It runs only on models that ask for it

explanation: goose uses structured log files with spans, not syslog triads.

miniLab.title: Architecture Dossier — module map + 3 find-and-explain traces
miniLab.instructions:
Write one markdown file `dossier.md` in your scratch dir containing:

A. A 1-page module map: for each of these modules one line each — crate-graph direction (l01), Message/MessageContentBlock home (l02), config singleton (l03), legacy loop entry (l04), state machine + one ops file (l05), Provider trait + one format file (l06), permission judge buckets (l07), extension registry (l08), MCP normalization (l09), compaction wiring (l10), exporter warning site (l11). Every line must cite a real file:line.

B. THREE find-and-explain traces, each 3-5 sentences with file:line evidence:
1. Trace GOOSE_MAX_TURNS from config read to enforcement in BOTH agent paths.
2. Trace one ToolRequest from provider stream to dispatch decision (mode gate -> inspection -> judge -> dispatch or skip).
3. Trace one Message from construction to persistence, one hop through the deserializer migration boundary.

Required intermediate terms in dossier.md: goose-provider-types, MessageContentBlock, StateMachine, GooseEffect, PermissionCheckResult, ExtensionManager, normalize_input_schema, compact_messages, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL.

Then run: powershell -File verify.ps1 -GooseRepo $env:GOOSE_REPO and paste the full output for auto-grading.
